title: Company-wide policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Marina Lopez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. These policies are intended to ensure security, compliance, fiscal discipline, and consistent operational practices across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private product teams.

Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors with Redwood systems access or who procure goods/services on behalf of Redwood. Exceptions require documented approval from the owner_team and Security/Finance as indicated in each section.

Owners & escalation
- Policy owner: people-ops (primary)
- Security owner (access & data controls): Security team
- Procurement & vendor contracts: Finance & Legal
- Travel approval policy: People Ops + Finance
- For questions or exceptions: policies@redwood.example (People Ops triage)

1) Access & Permissions (RBAC and lifecycle)

Principles:
- Least privilege by default: grant the minimal role needed for the job.
- Role-based access controls (RBAC) for services, with temporary exceptions only via just-in-time (JIT) access.
- Separation of duties for approval flows (requestor ≠ approver).
- Auditability: all privilege changes logged and reviewed monthly.

Roles & common mappings:
- viewer: read-only product dashboards, logs, documentation
- developer: standard code and staging infra access (no production keys)
- oncall: runbook/alert access, production debug tokens (time-limited)
- infra-admin: provisioning and network config (requires 2 approvers)
- sec-admin: security tooling and audit logs (Security team only)

Provisioning / Deprovisioning process (high-level):
1. Request: employee creates an access request in Access Portal (link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/access-portal) including justification and manager approval.
2. Approval: manager + resource owner approve. For elevated roles, require Security approval.
3. Provisioning: IAM team or automated workflow grants access; ticket recorded in Access Portal with change-id.
4. Review: monthly access review by team leads; exceptions > 30 days must be re-approved.
5. Offboarding: HR triggers deprovisioning within 24 hours of termination or contract end.

Emergency (break-glass) access:
- Emergency access requires a documented ticket, an owner-signed justification, and automatic revocation after 8 hours unless extended with Security approval. All actions performed using break-glass are recorded to an immutable audit log.

Automation & tooling:
- Use central IAM (cloud-provider IAM + company SSO) with SCIM for user provisioning.
- All privileged role grants must use MFA and hardware-backed keys for infra-admin/sec-admin.

SLOs & thresholds:
- Provisioning SLA: standard requests fulfilled within 48 business hours; elevated requests within 4 business hours.
- Deprovisioning SLA after HR notification: 24 hours.

2) Change Management (infra, runtime, and product changes)

Policy summary:
- All changes impacting production systems must go through the Change Request workflow unless classified as emergency changes in the incident process.
- Changes are classified as Minor, Major, or Critical with different approval matrices and windows.

Classification & approvals:
- Minor: configuration tweaks, docs, non-prod deployments. Approver: team lead. Scheduled during normal hours.
- Major: infra changes affecting availability (network, database schema migrations), model-serving changes with rollout. Approvers: owner_team, Eng SRE, and Product; window required off-peak.
- Critical: emergency security patches, incident-driven rollbacks. Approver: Incident Commander + Eng SRE + Security retroactive approval.

Standard change request template (use Change Request form):
- Title, Change-id, Owner, Risk assessment, Rollout plan, Backout plan, Monitoring & verification steps, Scheduled window, Approvers.

Change windows & cadence:
- Standard maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC for changes impacting Hosted.
- No Major changes during business-critical events or high-traffic product launches unless explicitly approved.

Rollback & verification:
1. Validate pre-change baseline snapshot (config + metrics).
2. Execute change and run verification checklist (latency, error-rate, throughput).
3. If verification fails, execute backout plan and open a post-change review.

Post-change review & audit:
- All Major and Critical changes require a postmortem within 5 business days and a changelog entry linking to the Change Request. Monthly change audit performed by Eng SRE.

3) Data Management (classification, retention, encryption, backups)

Data classification levels:
- Public: non-sensitive marketing materials.
- Internal: operational documents, internal metrics.
- Confidential: customer-identifiable metadata, internal product roadmaps.
- Restricted: regulated PII, customer data with contractual restrictions, keys/secrets.

Storage & encryption:
- All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest using KMS-managed keys and in transit with TLS 1.2+.
- Secrets must live in Vault/HSM integrations; never checked into source control.

Retention & deletion:
- Standard logs: 90 days (hot), 365 days (cold).
- Customer data: follow contractual TTL; default retention 7 years for audit-relevant records unless otherwise specified.
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) runbook; changes recorded and verified by Data Steward.

Backups & DR:
- Critical metadata/config backups: daily snapshot, 30-day rolling retention.
- Full backups for core databases: nightly with offsite replication; restore tested quarterly.

Data access requests:
- Request: submit Data Access Request (DAR) with business justification.
- Approval: Data Steward + Security approval for Restricted data.
- Access granted via temporary roles (JIT) and logged.

Data handling checklist for engineers:
- Sanitize logs before shipping externally.
- Use pseudonymization for datasets used for model evaluation.
- Use sandbox environments with synthetic or anonymized data for development.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Principles:
- Centralized procurement for large purchases; card-based petty expenses handled via expense system. Spend must follow approval tiers.

Approval tiers (examples):
- < $2,000: Manager approval
- $2,000–$25,000: Department head + Finance notification
- > $25,000: VP approval + Finance & Legal (PO/contract required)

Procurement flow (standard):
1. Request: submit a Purchase Request (PR) in Procurement Portal with cost center and justification.
2. Approval: approvers per tiers above.
3. PO & vendor onboarding: Finance issues PO; Legal runs contract review if > $10k or involves data processing.
4. Receipt & invoice: Accounts Payable (AP) matches invoice to PO; payment per vendor terms.

Card & expense policy:
- Use company card for approved travel and business expenses. Personal expenses are not permitted.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Expense submission deadline: within 30 days of transaction.

Compliance & audits:
- Finance conducts quarterly procurement audits for compliance and duplicate vendors.

5) Vendor Management & Contracting

Onboarding checklist:
- Vendor risk classification (Low / Medium / High) based on access to data, criticality, and regulatory scope.
- Security questionnaire for vendors with access to Redwood systems or data.
- Contract requirements: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) for vendors handling customer data, SLA definitions, liability caps, and termination clauses.

Vendor monitoring:
- Annual security attestations for Medium/High vendors.
- Quarterly operational health checks for vendors with critical infra dependencies.

Termination & offboarding:
- Revoke all vendor accounts and keys within 24 hours of contract termination.
- Validate data return or destruction per contract.

Escalation & remediation:
- If vendor security issues are detected, Security initiates a vendor incident workflow and coordinates with Legal and Product for impact assessment.

6) Travel policy (employee travel & expenses)

Booking & approvals:
- All business travel must be pre-approved in Travel Request form with estimated budget and approver.
- For international travel, Travel Request must include risk assessment and any visa/work permit considerations.

Allowable expenses & caps (examples):
- Flights: economy for domestic; premium economy for international travel >8 hours with manager approval.
- Lodging: up to $200/night in Tier-1 cities; check Travel Portal for approved hotels.
- Meals & incidentals: per-diem $75/day (domestic), $100/day (international).

Expense submission:
- Use Expense Portal to submit receipts within 30 days. Attach boarding passes, hotel folios, and itemized receipts.
- Personal leisure extensions must be declared and cost-split shown on the expense report.

Duty of care:
- People Ops maintains traveler contact lists and emergency procedures. For high-risk travel, Security will provide guidance and monitoring.

7) Internal templates & links

Available templates (use and customize per-team):
- Change Request template: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request-template
- Vendor Assessment & Security Questionnaire: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Travel Request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/travel-request-template
- Purchase Request (PR) form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates/purchase-request

Quick examples (copyable):
- Short change rollout checklist:
  1) Pre-change snapshot: configs, infra metrics
  2) Notify stakeholders (Slack #ops and #product)
  3) Execute change (document time)
  4) Run smoke tests: 95th latency, error-rate < 1%
  5) Confirm monitors green for 30 minutes, then close change ticket.

- Minimal DAR justification text (example):
  "Purpose: Access to analytics dataset for Q3 model evaluation. Scope: anonymized customer_event logs (no PII). Duration: 7 days. Reviewers: Data Steward, Security."

Governance & review cadence
- Policies are reviewed annually by People Ops with Security, Finance, Legal, and Eng SRE.
- Minor edits may be made as operational needs evolve; major policy changes require cross-team review and are communicated via All Hands and an update email with change highlights.

Compliance & enforcement
- Non-compliance reported to manager and owner_team. Repeated or severe violations will escalate to People Ops + Legal and may result in disciplinary action.
